subject: Pricing & technical tradeoffs for Optimize Toolkit pilot
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@NimbusOps.com>, Maya Patel <maya.p@NimbusOps.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 14:14:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing & technical tradeoffs for Optimize Toolkit pilot

Hi Sanjay / Maya —

Great talking yesterday. Per our conversation, I put together two quick packaging options for the Optimize toolkit pilot and attached a short set of technical artifacts (KV cache microbenchmarks + quantization accuracy summary) so you can see the expected delta on latency and token cost for your LLM workloads.

High level options:
- Pilot A (No commit): 30-day trial, 50k generated-token credits, standard support, no committed discount.
- Pilot B (Small commit): 3-month pilot, $25k committed spend, 20% usage credits back (applied as future credits), priority onboarding and a single on-site workshop (virtual ok).

We think the biggest lever for NimbusOps is caching: enabling prefix/KV caching for chat-style flows should reduce token consumption by ~30–40% for your common conversation patterns. Quantization (int8) can cut serving cost by another 25–35% on our Dedicated nodes with <2% measured accuracy drift in our benchmarks (see attached).

Questions for you so we can finalize the commercial:
1) Which pilot option aligns with procurement expectations?
2) Do you need stricter accuracy SLAs that would rule out int8 for the pilot?
3) Is NimbusOps procurement able to sign an MSA + SOW electronically (DocuSign) by the end of next week?

Attaching: kv_cache_benchmarks.pdf, quantization_accuracy_summary.xlsx, initial proposal (nimbusops_proposal_v2.pdf).

If helpful, happy to jump on a 30m call with your infra lead to walk the tradeoffs.

Thanks —
Mateo Alvarez
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@NimbusOps.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.p@NimbusOps.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing & technical tradeoffs for Optimize Toolkit pilot

Thanks Mateo — appreciate the level of detail. A few quick reactions and asks: 

- The KV cache numbers look promising; our primary concern is how cache invalidation behaves for our multi-tenant prompt templates. Would you be able to share a short note on invalidation semantics and hit rate expectations for templates with dynamic user inserts?
- On quantization: 2% drift is acceptable for most flows, but for our regulatory compliance flows we need to maintain a tighter fidelity. Can we scope those flows out of the pilot from a quantization perspective?
- Procurement: we can move fast on a 30-day trial but for any committed spend we need a PO template from Redwood and a standard vendor onboarding packet. I attached our internal procurement checklist.

Also — curious about how the 20% usage-credit back works in practice. Is that an up-front rebate or applied after invoice? That will determine how finance models the cost.

Happy to set a call with our infra lead (CCed Maya) on Friday if that helps.

Best,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform, NimbusOps
sanjay@NimbusOps.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@NimbusOps.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing & technical tradeoffs for Optimize Toolkit pilot

Hi Sanjay / Maya — looping in Marcus (commercial lead) to propose a practical commercial path based on your asks.

Short answers:
- Cache invalidation: Redwood's prefix/KV cache supports key-based TTLs and opaque cache keys derived from the canonicalized prompt + tenant id. For your dynamic templates we recommend a 10–30s TTL for session-level caches and explicit bust triggers when template parameters change. Our internal hit-rate for templates with stable prefixes is 60–75% in production; see kv_cache_benchmarks.pdf for sample distributions.
- Quantization scoping: absolutely — we can exclude regulatory flows from int8. We'll gate quantized variants behind a model tag so you can route sensitive traffic to higher-precision variants.

Commercial counterproposal (practical):
- Pilot: 60-day pilot with 75k generated-token credits + technical onboarding.
- If you convert to a 6-month committed package within the pilot window, Redwood will apply a 15% rebate on actual usage (applied as billing credit) and provide 3 months of extended analytics retention at no charge.
- For upfront PO simplicity: we can accept a PO against a simple MSA + SOW and apply the rebate after invoicing (so finance books the full spend and receives a subsequent credit).

Attachments we can provide to accelerate procurement:
- Standard PO template: Nimbus_PO_Template.docx
- Updated proposal PDF: nimbusops_proposal_v2.pdf (with revised credit/commit tiers)

Next steps suggested:
1) Mateo to send the gated MSA + SOW DocuSign link for signature (we'll pre-fill basic fields).
2) Marcus to schedule a 30m call with Maya + your infra lead to review cache semantics and quantization gating.
3) Procurement exchange: we can accept your PO and run the rebate credit as an invoice adjustment.

Marcus — can you confirm the 15% rebate is ok to commit to from commercial?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Commercials — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
